key_insight: SpikeDS uses dual sparsity—spike-based activation sparsity and window pruning—to make 3D MRI transformers more efficient while preserving performance for perineural invasion prediction.
clinical_relevance: This could help make volumetric MRI screening for perineural invasion more practical in cholangiocarcinoma by lowering compute and energy costs without sacrificing diagnostic accuracy.
method: Binary spiking neural network for 3D MRI analysis
Window-based Expert Mixture Spiking Attention (W-EMSA) selects salient windows using firing rates
Cross-Window Spiking Self-Attention (CW-SSA) lets pruned windows still provide global context
evidence_signal: In 139 cholangiocarcinoma patients with 5-fold cross-validation, SpikeDS achieved an AUC of 0.753 and used only 14.4 mJ, outperforming the best baseline on both accuracy and energy efficiency.
watch_item: The study is retrospective and single-cohort, so broader validation and deployment testing are needed before clinical use.
paper_title: SpikeDS: Dual Sparsity Spikformer for Perineural Invasion Prediction in 3D MRI
